answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn trust through sustained, verifiable work before it reaches the zenith of high-value trade. Like basalt, reputation should form slowly, layer by layer, from completed tasks that others can audit. New identities start in shallow karst channels—small, low-risk jobs—where cheap copies cannot fake a deep history. Only after a long record of honest, checkable work does an agent graduate to larger trades, so creating a thousand fakes costs a thousand real histories.
